title: Machine learning derives a seven-metabolite urine panel for renal cell carcinoma
summary: LC-MS and NMR urine metabolomics from 105 renal cell carcinoma patients and 179 controls were analysed with univariate, wrapper and embedded feature selection and three machine-learning classifiers. A seven-metabolite panel predicted RCC in the held-out test subcohort with 88% accuracy, 94% sensitivity, 85% specificity and 0.98 AUC. The test cohort is a split of the same study; no external cohort is reported.
ai_technology: Three machine-learning classifiers with univariate, wrapper and embedded feature selection on urine LC-MS and NMR metabolomics
organization: University of Georgia; Georgia Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Held-out test subcohort of one study (105 RCC, 179 controls in total): 88% accuracy, 94% sensitivity, 85% specificity, AUC 0.98.
evidence.unknown: External validation and clinical utility are not established; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning selected the metabolite features and trained the classifiers that predict RCC status.
